lessons.title: Creating a Simple Flyer or Poster
lessons.body: A flyer or poster is one of the cheapest ways to advertise your business. In Spanish, you need a few key phrases. Start with a headline: 'Â¡Oferta especial!' (Special offer!) or 'Â¡Nuevo!' (New!). Then describe your product: 'Vendo camisetas de algodÃ³n' (I sell cotton t-shirts). Add your location: 'Estamos en el mercado central' (We are at the central market). Include a phone number: 'Llama al 123-456-789' (Call 123-456-789). Use big, bold letters for the headline and your phone number. In many African countries, Spanish is spoken in Equatorial Guinea, but you might also use Spanish to attract customers from Spanish-speaking countries or for tourism. If you're in a tourist area, bilingual flyers work well. For example, in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea, you might write: 'Â¡Prueba nuestro pescado fresco! Fresh fish!' Use bright colors like yellow, red, and green. Print at a local print shop for about 100-200 CFA francs per copy (or equivalent in your currency). Distribute at markets, churches, and community centers. You can also make a digital flyer using Canva (free app) and share on WhatsApp. Keep text short: 5-10 words per line. Use action words: 'Compra' (Buy), 'Visita' (Visit), 'Ahorra' (Save). Add a special offer: '2 por 1' (2 for 1). Always include a call to action: 'Â¡Ven hoy!' (Come today!). Practice writing a flyer for your own business. Remember: correct spelling matters. Double-check accents: 'mÃ¡s' (more) vs 'mas' (but). Use a dictionary or Google Translate to verify. A good flyer can bring 10-20 new customers per week if placed in high-traffic areas.

lessons.title: Describing Your Business in One Sentence
lessons.body: You need a one-sentence pitch in Spanish to tell people what you do. This is called an 'elevator pitch'. Start with 'Somos' (We are) or 'Vendo' (I sell). For example: 'Vendo ropa usada de buena calidad a precios bajos' (I sell good quality second-hand clothes at low prices). Or 'Ofrecemos servicios de peluquerÃ­a a domicilio' (We offer hairdressing services at home). Keep it under 15 words. Include what you sell, who you serve, and why you're different. For a food business: 'Preparamos comida casera africana para eventos' (We prepare homemade African food for events). For a farm: 'Cultivamos tomates orgÃ¡nicos sin quÃ­micos' (We grow organic tomatoes without chemicals). Practice saying it clearly and confidently. In Spanish, adjectives usually come after the noun: 'ropa barata' (cheap clothes), not 'barata ropa'. Use 'para' (for) to show your target: 'para estudiantes' (for students). Use 'con' (with) to show a feature: 'con entrega gratis' (with free delivery). Write your sentence on a card and memorize it. Test it on friends: do they understand? If not, simplify. You can also use it on social media bio, business cards, and flyers. For example, in Accra, Ghana, a tailor might say: 'Hago vestidos a medida para mujeres profesionales' (I make custom dresses for professional women). In Nairobi, Kenya, a tech repair shop: 'Reparo telÃ©fonos y computadoras rÃ¡pidamente' (I repair phones and computers quickly). Always end with a smile and eye contact. This sentence opens conversations and closes sales.

lessons.title: Social Media Posts for Your Products
lessons.body: Social media is powerful for small businesses. In Spanish, a good post has a photo, a short caption, and a call to action. Use platforms like WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok. For WhatsApp status, post a photo of your product with text: 'Â¡Disponible hoy! Zapatos de cuero, talla 38-42. 15.000 FCFA. EnvÃ­o gratis en Malabo.' (Available today! Leather shoes, size 38-42. 15,000 CFA. Free delivery in Malabo.) Use hashtags: #Oferta #Moda #NegocioLocal. On Facebook, write longer: 'Â¿Buscas un regalo? Tenemos cestas tejidas a mano. Hechas en Ghana. Precio: 5.000 FCFA. Pide por WhatsApp: 123-456-789.' (Looking for a gift? We have hand-woven baskets. Made in Ghana. Price: 5,000 CFA. Order via WhatsApp: 123-456-789.) Post 3-5 times a week. Best times: 7-9 AM and 7-9 PM. Use emojis: ðï¸ð±ð°. Respond to comments in Spanish: 'Gracias' (Thank you), 'SÃ­, tenemos' (Yes, we have). For Instagram, use Stories with polls: 'Â¿Prefieres rojo o azul?' (Do you prefer red or blue?). For TikTok, make a 15-second video showing your product in use. Speak simple Spanish: 'Mira esto' (Look at this), 'Es fÃ¡cil' (It's easy). Always include price and how to buy. Example: 'Solo 10 unidades. EnvÃ­a un mensaje para pedir.' (Only 10 units. Send a message to order.) Track what works: if a post gets many likes, do more like that. Use free tools like Canva for graphics. Remember: consistency beats perfection. A daily post with a clear photo and price will bring sales.

lessons.title: Word-of-Mouth Marketing Phrases
lessons.body: Word-of-mouth is the oldest and cheapest marketing. In Spanish, you need phrases to ask for referrals and to thank customers. After a sale, say: 'Si te gusta, cuÃ©ntale a un amigo' (If you like it, tell a friend). Or 'RecomiÃ©ndanos y recibe un descuento' (Recommend us and get a discount). Give a small reward: 'Trae un amigo y ambos reciben 10% de descuento' (Bring a friend and both get 10% off). Use these phrases in daily interactions. When someone compliments your product, respond: 'Â¡Gracias! Â¿Conoces a alguien que tambiÃ©n lo necesite?' (Thanks! Do you know someone who also needs it?). For services, ask: 'Â¿Puedes dejar una reseÃ±a en Google?' (Can you leave a review on Google?). In African markets, trust is key. Speak with respect: use 'usted' for older customers, 'tÃº' for peers. Example in Equatorial Guinea: 'DoÃ±a MarÃ­a, si le gusta el pescado, dÃ­gale a sus vecinas. Tenemos entrega a domicilio.' (Mrs. Maria, if you like the fish, tell your neighbors. We have home delivery.) Also, create a simple referral card: 'Recomienda a un amigo y obtÃ©n 500 FCFA de descuento en tu prÃ³xima compra.' (Recommend a friend and get 500 CFA off your next purchase.) Train your employees to say: 'Gracias por su compra. Â¡Vuelva pronto!' (Thanks for your purchase. Come back soon!). Word-of-mouth works best when you exceed expectations. Give a little extra: 'Un regalo pequeÃ±o por tu compra' (A small gift for your purchase). Ask for feedback: 'Â¿QuÃ© podemos mejorar?' (What can we improve?). Happy customers become your best advertisers. In a study by Nielsen, 92% of people trust recommendations from friends over ads. So, focus on making each customer a promoter.

lessons.title: Promotional Offers and Special Deals
lessons.body: Promotions drive quick sales. In Spanish, use clear, urgent phrases. Common offers: '2x1' (two for one), '3 por 2' (three for two), 'Descuento del 20%' (20% discount), 'EnvÃ­o gratis' (free shipping), 'Precio especial' (special price). For a limited time: 'Solo hoy' (only today), 'VÃ¡lido hasta el viernes' (valid until Friday), 'Ãltimas unidades' (last units). Create a sense of urgency: 'Â¡Date prisa!' (Hurry!). For loyalty: 'Tarjeta de fidelidad: compra 5, lleva 1 gratis' (Loyalty card: buy 5, get 1 free). For holidays: 'Oferta de Navidad' (Christmas offer), 'Especial RamadÃ¡n' (Ramadan special). Use numbers: 'Ahorra 2.000 FCFA' (Save 2,000 CFA). In African markets, bundle deals work well: 'Paquete familiar: 5 kg de arroz + 2 litros de aceite por 10.000 FCFA' (Family pack: 5 kg rice + 2 liters oil for 10,000 CFA). Advertise on WhatsApp, flyers, and in-person. When a customer hesitates, say: 'Si compras ahora, te doy un 10% de descuento' (If you buy now, I'll give you 10% off). But don't devalue your product. Use promotions sparinglyâonce a month. Track results: did sales increase? If not, change the offer. Example: a salon in Kigali, Rwanda, offered 'Martes de descuento: 30% en trenzas' (Discount Tuesday: 30% off braids) and saw a 40% increase in Tuesday customers. Always state conditions: 'VÃ¡lido de lunes a miÃ©rcoles' (Valid Monday to Wednesday). Be honest: don't say 'gratis' if it's not. Use 'sin costo adicional' (no extra cost) for add-ons. Practice writing three offers for your business in Spanish.

lessons.title: Practice: Write a Social Media Ad for Your Business
lessons.body: Now it's time to write your own social media ad in Spanish. Follow this template. First, choose a platform: WhatsApp, Facebook, or Instagram. Write a headline: 'Â¡Oferta imperdible!' (Unmissable offer!) or 'Â¡Nuevo producto!' (New product!). Then describe your product or service in one sentence: 'Vendo miel pura de abejas de las montaÃ±as de Kenia.' (I sell pure honey from the mountains of Kenya.) Add a benefit: 'Ideal para la salud y la energÃ­a.' (Ideal for health and energy.) State the price: '500 ml por solo 3.000 FCFA.' (500 ml for only 3,000 CFA.) Include a call to action: 'Pide ahora por WhatsApp: 123-456-789.' (Order now via WhatsApp: 123-456-789.) Add a hashtag: #MielNatural #Kenia #Salud. Use emojis: ð¯ðªð². Post a clear photo of your product. For a video ad, show yourself using it: 'Mira quÃ© rica' (Look how delicious). Keep it under 30 seconds. Write in simple Spanish. Avoid long sentences. Use 'tÃº' for informal, 'usted' for formal. If you're targeting a wider audience, use 'ustedes'. Check your spelling. Use Google Translate to verify, but ask a Spanish speaker if possible. In Equatorial Guinea, you can find Spanish speakers. In other African countries, look for language exchange groups on Facebook. Practice by writing three versions: one for WhatsApp status, one for Facebook post, one for Instagram caption. Share with a friend and ask: 'Â¿Entiendes quÃ© vendo y cÃ³mo comprar?' (Do you understand what I sell and how to buy?). If not, revise. Finally, post it and track responses. Even one sale means success. Repeat weekly. Over time, you'll build a Spanish-speaking customer base.

quiz.q: What is the Spanish phrase for 'Special offer!'?
quiz.explanation: Â¡Oferta especial! directly translates to 'Special offer!'

quiz.q: How do you say 'Call 123-456-789' in Spanish?
quiz.explanation: Llama al means 'Call to' in Spanish.

quiz.q: Which word means 'Buy' as a command?
quiz.explanation: Compra is the imperative form of 'comprar' (to buy).

quiz.q: What does '2 por 1' mean?
quiz.explanation: Por means 'for' in this context, so 2 por 1 is '2 for 1'.

quiz.q: How do you say 'Come today!' in Spanish?
quiz.explanation: Ven is the imperative of 'venir' (to come).

quiz.q: Which phrase means 'We are'?
quiz.explanation: Somos is the first-person plural of 'ser' (to be) for permanent states.

quiz.q: What is the correct order for 'cheap clothes' in Spanish?
quiz.explanation: In Spanish, adjectives usually follow the noun, so 'ropa barata'.

quiz.q: How do you say 'for students'?
quiz.explanation: Para means 'for' when indicating a target audience.

quiz.q: What does 'con entrega gratis' mean?
quiz.explanation: Con means 'with', entrega means 'delivery', gratis means 'free'.

quiz.q: Which sentence means 'I make custom dresses for professional women'?

quiz.explanation: Hago vestidos a medida para mujeres profesionales is the correct translation.
